messages:
sasha: Quick RFC follow-up — prototyped a small loader extension I called 'mini-hydration' that does layerwise progressive hydration + a tiny signed-chunk header (opt-in). POC numbers: ~8–12% p99 improvement for short completions on the 7B family when prefix cache hit rate is low. Posting sketch and questions.

ben: cool! can you summarize the tradeoffs? signature verification per-chunk worries me (CPU overhead), but progressive hydration sounds promising for cold starts.

sasha: tradeoffs: 1) extra 24B header per chunk (base64 sig + nonce) — small on disk but adds a few ms on first read; 2) verifying every chunk deterministically prevents silent tampering but we can defer full sig verification until after hydration completes (verify root chain first) to avoid blocking on IO; 3) loader API complexity increases slightly.

jen: API suggestion (pseudo):
```
# new loader surface on ModelLoader
def hydrate_layer(layer_id: str, mode: str = 'lazy', priority: int = 5) -> Future[ShardHandle]:
    """mode in ['eager','lazy','prefetch']
    returns handle that resolves when layer bytes are resident or when fallback kicks in"""
```
Keep it minimal. If 'prefetch' we can kick async read+decompress+cache; 'lazy' reads on demand.

liam: rollout concerns: we should canary on Dedicated first (predictable IO). Metrics to watch: warmup_io_bytes, shard_miss_rate, first_token_latency, verification_cpu_ms, and OOM spikes. Add a kill-switch env var for on-the-fly disabling.

ben: Another thought — expose a compact format discriminator byte in the safetensors header so older loaders gracefully ignore the extra fields. That keeps backwards compatibility. Also we should version the header: v1 = no mini-hydration, v2 = optional hyd_hint.

sasha: agreed on versioning. Proposed header sketch: {"fmt_v": "2", "hyd_hint": {"layer_map": [...], "root_sig": "base64"}} — optional. We won't require a sidecar manifest.

jen: love avoiding sidecars. For security: do root_sig verification on the control path (cheap), then optionally queue full chunk verification as lower-priority background tasks that mark a shard 'verified' in metadata when done. If a chunk fails verification while in use, fallback to redelivery of shard from origin.

liam: ops checklist: 1) canary config + gradual ramp, 2) add telemetry tags: hyd_mode, hyd_priority, hyd_verified=true/false, 3) instrument memory accounting per-hydrated-layer, 4) add eviction policy tweaks so partially hydrated layers don't block smaller models.

sasha: implementation plan: small loader change + compat header bump. I'll open a tiny RFC with code snippets and perf numbers. Can folks +1 if they're ok with trying a canary next week?

ben: +1 from me. Would like a quick microbenchmark harness to replay short prompt tails and a flag to force eager verification for test runs.

jen: +1. I'll add unit tests for header parsing and a fake-verifier mode to simulate verification latency.

liam: +1, ops will set up the canary deployment and dashboards. Add a rollback playbook entry.

warmup-bot: scheduled warmup-canary job for canary cluster 'dedicated-canary-3' in 24h. Check /ops/warmups for logs. :robot_face:

sasha: thanks team — I'll post the RFC link and draft patch later today. If anyone has strong objections to header-in-band (vs sidecar) speak up now; otherwise I'll proceed with v2 header + loader opt-in flag.
